summary: PSDS lens result: the Leech-tree problem is the tree-shaped member of the perfect-systems-of-difference-sets family, but the classical nonexistence machinery does NOT import wholesale, for two precisely identifiable reasons. (1) A spider Leech tree is a threshold-1 PSDS only after deleting the cross-leg SUM values: its m difference triangles must tile [1,N] minus the (1-Theta(1/m))-dense set of cross-sums, so every interval-tiling theorem (BKT 1978, Kotzig-Turgeon 1977/1980) fails to apply for m>=3 legs; for m<=2 legs the reduction is literal and reproves only the known 'no Leech path n>=5'. (2) I re-derived the Bermond-Kotzig-Turgeon small-difference counting (top-row and r-layer counts) and showed it is identically vacuous at threshold c=1 - it proves exactly m>=2c-1 - so even without the sum-holes it would kill nothing; the unique threshold-free PSDS tool, nonexistence of all (m,k,c)-PSDS with k>=6 (BKT 1978 Prop 2.1-2.2; Kotzig-Turgeon 1977 for (v,k,1)-PDFs; quantitatively strengthened Aug 2026: t-mark Golomb-ruler difference packings almost-cover [1,U] iff 3<=t<=5, arXiv 2608.13739), is powered by the Sidon deficiency of PATHS, which is exactly what bushy trees evade (B_{2,2} is a 6-vertex tree component achieving what no 6-mark ruler can). What DOES transfer is the proof technique: I adapted the component-counting to general trees and proved (machine-checked on all five known Leech trees, script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-geoclaw-Documents/a128be0a-cd3b-4a92-82b6-f91337915fb0/scratchpad/check_psds_claims.py) a component-refined forcing inequality w_{k+1} <= 1 + sum_i C(e_i+1,2) (tight in L6 and L4_path), a connectivity corollary (near-tight forcing forces the k lightest edges to be a subtree), and a rigidity ladder: w_{k+1}=C(k+1,2)+1 iff the k lightest edges form a Leech tree of order k+1, whence w_q <= C(q,2) (improving Calhoun by 1) for every q<=min(n-1,24), q not in {2,3,4,6}, in every Leech tree of every order, plus the branching anchor 'w_6=16 forces F_5 = L6 exactly'. The Kloeve/Lorentzen-Nilsen/Shearer difference-triangle-set scope bounds import validly (M(I,J)<=N for I disjoint J-edge paths) but are provably dominated by the vertex count and the single-path Golomb bound already in the repo. Net reframe: Leech(n) exists iff Calhoun's M(n)=C(n,2) (zero tree-Golomb deficiency); the PSDS-native route forward is a tree analog of the Kotzig-Turgeon 'petites composantes' / 2026 almost-covering-threshold theorems for perfect distance forests. Key sources: [PSDS+PDF survey 2025](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20446), [PDF constructions survey](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.10367), [almost-covering threshold 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13739), [Shearer LP bounds EJC 1999](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v6i1r31/pdf), [Kotzig-Turgeon 1977](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0012365X77900644), [Ge-Miao-Sun 2010](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/jcd.20259).

claims.name: I1. Imported definitions and theorem inventory (PSDS/PDF), with exact statements
claims.statement: Definition (BKT 1978): an (m,{p_1,...,p_m},c)-PSDS is a family S_1..S_m of integer sets, |S_i|=p_i, such that the multiset union of positive differences Delta+S_i equals {c, c+1, ..., c-1+sum_i C(p_i,2)} exactly. A (v,k,1)-PDF is a regular ((v-1)/(k(k-1)), k, 1)-PSDS. Confirmed theorems: (T1) [Kotzig-Turgeon, Discrete Math 20 (1977) 249-254] no (v,k,1)-PDF exists for k>=6; for k=5, v==21 (mod 40) and v in {41,81} are excluded; for k=4, v in {25,37} excluded; for k=3, v==13,19 (mod 24) excluded. (T2) [Bermond-Kotzig-Turgeon, Colloq. Math. Soc. Janos Bolyai 18 (1978) 135-149, Props 2.1-2.2] if an (m,4,c)-PSDS exists then m>=2c-1; NO (m,k,c)-PSDS exists for ANY k>=6, m>=1, c>=1. (T3) [Bermond-Brouwer-Germa, Colloq. CNRS 260 (1978) 35-38] (m,3,c)-PSDS requires m>=2c-1 with m==0,1 (mod 4) if c odd, m==0,3 (mod 4) if c even; [D. G. Rogers] this is sufficient (full spectrum). (T4) (m,5,c)-PSDS requires m>=4c (as quoted in the 2025 survey arXiv:2510.20446, Prop 1.2). (T5) existence: (v,3,1)-PDF iff v==1,7 (mod 24) (Skolem 1957 / KT 1977 / BBG 1978); (v,4,lambda)-PDF iff lambda(v-1)==0 (mod 12), v>=13, (v,lambda) not in {(25,1),(37,1)} (Liu-Feng-Wang-Zhang 2025, settling Bermond's conjecture). (T6) [Kotzig-Turgeon, Ann. Discrete Math. 8 (1980) 71-75, 'Sur l'existence de petites composantes dans tout systeme parfait d'ensembles de differences'] every perfect system of difference sets contains a small component (title-level; exact numeric bound not re-verified, see open questions).
claims.proof_sketch: Literature import, not proved here. Statements cross-confirmed verbatim from two independent modern surveys (arXiv:2510.20446 Def 1.3, Props 1.1-1.2, Thms 1.1-1.5; arXiv:2110.10367 p.2, which states 'In [6,15] it is proved that perfect difference families cannot exist for k>=6' with [6]=BKT 1978, [15]=KT 1980) and by arXiv:2608.13739 (2026), which cites the same classical nonexistence. Primary 1970s texts are paywalled (ScienceDirect/Springer/zbMATH all 403'd); I could not re-derive the k>=6 proof. The m>=2c-1 bound I did re-derive independently (see claim A1). CAUTION for the ledger: label T1/T2 LITERATURE-ONLY, T6 UNCLEAR (title-level), T3/T5 LITERATURE-ONLY, T4 LITERATURE-ONLY (single survey source).

claims.name: A0. Spider correspondence: exact statement and the exact obstruction to a PSDS reduction
claims.statement: Let T be a spider with centre v0 and legs of edge-lengths k_1..k_m (n = 1 + sum k_i, N = C(n,2)), and let S_i = {0, a_{i,1}, ..., a_{i,k_i}} be the cumulative distances from v0 along leg i. Then T is a Leech tree IFF (i) each S_i is a Golomb ruler; (ii) the difference triangles Delta+S_1, ..., Delta+S_m are pairwise disjoint; (iii) the C(m,2)-fold cross-sum multiset CS = {a+b : a in S_i\{0}, b in S_j\{0}, i<j} is repeat-free and disjoint from union_i Delta+S_i; (iv) (union_i Delta+S_i) disjoint-union CS = {1,...,N}. Hence a spider Leech tree is an (m,{k_i+1},1)-PSDS *with prescribed holes exactly at the cross-sums*. For m=1,2 (CS empty or the spider is a path through v0) the correspondence is literal: Leech path on n vertices = (1,{n},1)-PSDS = perfect ruler, which by T1 (or classically) exists only for n<=4 - reproving repo lemma L3 via PSDS. For m>=3, |CS| = sum_{i<j} k_i k_j = (1 - Theta(1/m)) N for balanced legs, so the difference triangles tile a subset of [1,N] of density only ~1/m: NO interval-tiling (PSDS) nonexistence theorem applies. The PSDS axioms hold verbatim only on the initial segment [1, q0) where q0 = min_{i<j}(a_{i,1}+a_{j,1}) = sum of the two smallest centre-incident weights, which can be as small as 3.
claims.proof_sketch: Distances within leg i together with distances from v0 are exactly Delta+S_i (v0 is the mark 0); distances across legs i,j are a_{i,s}+a_{j,t}; the counting identity sum_i C(k_i+1,2) + sum_{i<j} k_i k_j = C(1+sum k_i, 2) shows (i)-(iv) exhaust the Leech condition. Machine-checked (script check_psds_claims.py): L4_star = triangles {1},{2},{4} + cross-sums {3,5,6}; L4_path viewed at its internal fork = triangles {1},{2,3,5} + cross-sums {4,6}; P4 as ruler {0,1,4,6}.
claims.checkable_prediction: For any spider topology in data/trees_18.jsonl, a Leech labelling would give 3+ disjoint Golomb rulers sharing the interval [1,153] with the density split above; the q0-window statement predicts the forced-weight search on spiders behaves exactly like a PSDS component search until the first cross-sum, then diverges - visible in Calhoun-style search traces.

claims.name: A1. Calibration: BKT small-difference counting is identically vacuous at threshold c=1
claims.statement: Re-derivation of the BKT machinery with exact quantifiers: in any (m,{p_i},c)-PSDS with A = sum_i (p_i - 1) top-row (adjacent) differences and D = sum_i C(p_i,2) total differences, (a) the sum of all top-row entries equals the sum of the m per-component maxima, giving Ac + C(A,2)... precisely: sum of the A smallest covered values <= sum of top rows = sum of component maxima <= sum of the m largest covered values, which simplifies for regular systems (p_i = q+1) to c <= (m+1)/2, i.e. exactly BKT's m >= 2c-1; and (b) the r-layer count ('values in [c,(r+1)c) lie in the top r rows') gives rc <= sum_i sum_{j<=min(r,p_i-1)} (p_i - j). At c=1 BOTH families of inequalities reduce to (m-1)(q-1) >= 0 and r <= (top-r row count), true for every size vector: the entire BKT counting apparatus proves nothing at threshold 1. Consistently, threshold-1 multi-component systems exist in abundance (Skolem: (m,3,1)-PSDS iff m==0,1 mod 4). Consequence: the ONLY threshold-free PSDS nonexistence tool is the k>=6 theorem (T2), whose mechanism is the positive-fraction Sidon deficiency of rulers (a t-mark ruler needs length ~t^2 but contributes only C(t,2) ~ t^2/2 differences), NOT interval-crowding.
claims.proof_sketch: Top-row argument: each component's maximal difference equals its top-row sum; all differences are distinct values in [c, c+D-1]; sum the A smallest values below, the m largest above; algebra (done twice, symbolically) yields c <= (m+1)/2 for regular systems and -(q-1)(m-1) <= 0 at c=1 for mixed sizes. Layer argument: a difference in [c,(r+1)c) is a sum of at most r adjacent differences (each >= c), hence lies in rows 1..r; row capacities give the inequality; at c=1 the interval [1, r+1) contains r values vs top-r capacity >= r. This also explains why the repo's forcing lemma (mex cascade) is the correct and complete c=1 analog: it is the exact, value-by-value version of the layer count.
claims.checkable_prediction: Any claimed 'import' of BKT counting that purports to constrain Leech trees (c=1) beyond the forcing lemma must fail on the Skolem witness family: e.g. the (4,3,1)-PSDS {0,1,5},{0,2,8},{0,3,10},{0,9,21} - wait, verify any standard Skolem split of [1,12] into 4 triples a+b=c; such families satisfy every BKT inequality with slack, checkable instantly.

claims.name: A2. Component-refined forcing inequality (tree transplant of the PSDS component count)
claims.statement: Let T be a Leech tree of order n with weights w_1 < ... < w_{n-1}, and for 1 <= k <= n-2 let F_k be the forest of the k lightest edges, with tree components having e_1 >= ... >= e_{m_k} >= 1 edges (sum e_i = k). Then w_{k+1} <= 1 + sum_i C(e_i+1, 2) <= 1 + C(k-m_k+2, 2) + (m_k - 1). The first inequality is attained with equality in real Leech trees: L6 at k=3 (components {1,2},{4}: bound 1+3+1=5=w_4) and L4_path at k=2 (components {1},{2}: bound 3=w_3). Calhoun's corollary w_{k+1} <= C(k+1,2)+1 is the m_k=1 case.
claims.proof_sketch: Every value v in [1, w_{k+1}-1] is a distance (Leech), and its path uses only edges of weight <= v < w_{k+1}, i.e. lies inside one component of F_k; distinct values are distinct vertex pairs; a component with e_i edges has C(e_i+1,2) pairs. The second bound is convexity (extremal size vector (k-m+1,1,...,1)). This is exactly the PSDS argument 'the downward-closed family of small windows in each component is counted by C(s_i+1,2)' transplanted from ruler components to tree components. Machine-checked for all k on all five known Leech trees (script check_psds_claims.py, all pass).
claims.checkable_prediction: In the n=18 (and future n=25) forced-weight searches, every partial forest must satisfy w_{k+1} <= 1 + sum C(e_i+1,2) at every step - a pruning rule strictly finer than Calhoun's whenever the current forest is disconnected; violations should already be implicitly absent in Calhoun-style search traces, testable by instrumenting the existing engine.

claims.name: A3. Connectivity corollary: near-tight forcing makes the light edges cluster
claims.statement: In any Leech tree, for every k >= 2: if w_{k+1} >= C(k,2) + 3 then m_k = 1, i.e. the k lightest edges form a connected subtree. (Contrapositive of A2: m_k >= 2 implies w_{k+1} <= 1 + C(k,2) + 1 = C(k,2)+2.) Interpretation: whenever the mex-cascade runs 'hot' (close to its C(k+1,2)+1 ceiling), the small-weight edges cannot be scattered - the PSDS phenomenon 'few components at the small end' holds for trees in this exact conditional form.
claims.proof_sketch: Immediate from A2 with m_k >= 2. Checked on the five known trees: the hypothesis w_{k+1} >= C(k,2)+3 triggers only where F_k is indeed connected (L4_star k=2: w_3 = 4 = C(2,2)+3, F_2 connected).
claims.checkable_prediction: Concrete search anchor at every order: if the search branch places edges 1 and 2 non-adjacent (m_2 = 2), then w_3 = 3 (<= C(2,2)+2 = 3 forced); if adjacent, w_3 = 4; at k=5, a branch with w_6 >= 13 = C(5,2)+3 must have its five lightest edges connected - directly testable against results/theory_filters_18.jsonl search states.

claims.name: A4. Rigidity ladder: tight forcing = Leech subtree; unconditional -1 improvements at 19 indices
claims.statement: (a) For every Leech tree and every k >= 1: w_{k+1} = C(k+1,2)+1 IF AND ONLY IF F_k is connected and is itself a Leech tree of order k+1 (its distance set is exactly {1,...,C(k+1,2)}). (b) Combining with the known order exclusions (Taylor parity for non-admissible orders; SWZ 2005 for 9,11; Calhoun 2007 for 16; this project for 18; the five known trees are the only Leech trees of order <= 24): in EVERY Leech tree of EVERY order n, for every q with 5 <= q <= min(n-1, 24) and q not in {6}: w_q <= C(q,2), improving the Calhoun bound C(q,2)+1 by exactly 1 at the 19 indices q in {5,7,8,...,24}. (c) Rigid branching anchors at the exceptional indices: w_6 = 16 forces F_5 to be the unique order-6 Leech tree B_{2,2} with weights {1,2,5;4,8}; w_4 = 7 forces F_3 = K_{1,3} weighted (1,2,4); w_3 = 4 forces edges 1,2 adjacent. (d) Self-improving ladder: every future order exclusion q (25, 27, 36, ...) automatically propagates 'w_q <= C(q,2)' into all higher-order searches.
claims.proof_sketch: (a) Forward: by A2, equality forces m_k = 1 (for m_k >= 2 the cap is C(k,2)+2 < C(k+1,2)+1 when k >= 2) and forces all C(k+1,2) pairs of the subtree to realise exactly [1, C(k+1,2)]; backward: if F_k is Leech of order k+1 its mex is C(k+1,2)+1, which is w_{k+1} by the forcing lemma. (b) If w_q = C(q,2)+1 then a Leech tree of order q exists inside T - contradiction for the excluded q. This is the exact tree analog of the PSDS proof-shape 'exact tiling of an initial segment forces a sub-perfect-system'. Machine-checked: on the five known trees every equality instance (w_2 always; w_3=4 in L4_star, L6; w_4=7 in L4_star) verifies that F_k is Leech (script output RIGID lines all True).
claims.checkable_prediction: At n=18: w_5 <= 10, w_7 <= 21, w_8 <= 28, ..., w_14 <= 91 (the q <= 14 cases bite below the Calhoun edge cap m_1 <= 105); and every search branch reaching w_6 = 16 must have placed exactly the B_{2,2}(1,2,5;4,8) configuration - both statements are directly checkable against the frozen n=18 forced-forest search and will prune at n=25 (where w_24 <= 276 also applies).

claims.name: A5. Hop-layer inequality (tree analog of the BKT row count)
claims.statement: In any Leech tree, for every r >= 1 and every t < w_1 + w_2 + ... + w_{r+1} (sum of the r+1 smallest weights): t <= sum_{h=1}^{r} P_h(F(t)), where F(t) is the forest of edges of weight <= t and P_h counts h-edge paths in it. Specializations: r=1 gives (w_1,w_2)=(1,2) (repo L1); r=2 gives t <= k(t) + sum_v C(deg_{F(t)}(v), 2) for all t < w_1+w_2+w_3 <= 7 - full coverage of the initial segment requires the small-weight core to supply 2-hop pairs, i.e. local bushiness, complementing the global degree cap (star-Sidon Delta <= 11 at n=18) from the opposite side.
claims.proof_sketch: A path with >= r+1 edges has weight >= w_1+...+w_{r+1} > t, so every value <= t is realised with hop <= r inside F(t); count paths by hop length. This is the value-window version of the PSDS layer inequality (claim A1(b)) with 'rows' = hop counts. Machine-checked for r = 1,2 on the five known trees. Its asymptotic extension (if forcing stays within a constant factor of tight up to scale K, the core must have average small-distance hop count growing like k^{1/3}, forcing spider/broom-like cores of hop-diameter <~ k^{2/3}) reproduces the repo's 'bushy but not star-like' middle regime from the difference side alone - that extension is only a sketch, not a theorem.

claims.name: A6. Difference-triangle-set import: valid but dominated (closed channel)
claims.statement: If a Leech tree of order n contains I vertex-disjoint paths with J edges each, then Kloeve's minimum scope satisfies M(I,J) <= N = C(n,2), because the I cumulative-mark sets form an (I,J) difference triangle set (all within-path distances are distinct tree distances, all <= N). Exact imported values: M(2,9)=121, M(3,7)=100, M(5,5)=79 (Shearer 1999, correcting Kloeve's claimed M(5,5)=83), M(9,4)=91; LP lower-bound families M(I,5) >= (91I+6)/6, M(I,6) >= (179I+9)/8; full LP table for I <= 15, J <= 20 (Shearer, Electron. J. Combin. 6 (1999) #R31, extending Lorentzen-Nilsen, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 37 (1991) 1486-1488; definitions from Kloeve, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 35 (1989)). HOWEVER: at n = 18 every instance is vacuous - the first violated bound M(2,11) >= 161 > 153 would need 24 > 18 vertices - and asymptotically M(I,J) ~ I J^2/2 (1+epsilon_J) with small epsilon for I >= 2, so the constraint M(I,J) <= C(n,2) is implied by I(J+1) <= n up to the epsilon; only the I = 1 case (single path = Golomb ruler, factor-2 Sidon gain) bites, and that is exactly the repo's existing L6 diameter bound. Verdict: record and close.
claims.proof_sketch: The reduction is one line (disjoint paths + global distance distinctness + scope <= N); the domination argument compares the LP bounds' linear-in-I growth (91/6 vs trivial 15 for J=5: 1.1% gain) with the quadratic single-ruler gain, plus the vertex-count constraint I(J+1) <= n. Literature values not re-derived here (Shearer's table read directly from the open-access PDF, archived at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-geoclaw-Documents/a128be0a-cd3b-4a92-82b6-f91337915fb0/scratchpad/dts_lp.txt).
claims.checkable_prediction: For all n <= 40 and all (I,J) with I(J+1) <= n and I >= 2, Shearer's table satisfies M(I,J) <= C(n,2) - i.e. the channel never fires; a 20-line script against the archived table verifies this.

claims.name: A7. Deficiency reframe: Leech(n) iff M(n) = C(n,2), and where the k>=6 mechanism dies for trees
claims.statement: Define delta(n) = M(n) - C(n,2) >= 0, where M(n) is Calhoun's minimum possible largest distance of a distinct-distance tree on n vertices ('tree-Golomb deficiency'). Then: a Leech tree of order n exists IFF delta(n) = 0. The PSDS k>=6 collapse (T1/T2) and the 2026 almost-covering threshold (arXiv:2608.13739, Thm 1.1: families of t-mark Golomb rulers with disjoint difference sets in [1,U] cover U - o(U) values iff 3 <= t <= 5, with a positive-density gap for t >= 6) are both powered by the PATH deficiency G(m) - C(m,2) ~ m^2/2 being a positive fraction of the scope (Sidon). Trees evade this mechanism: known values give delta(2)=delta(3)=delta(4)=delta(6)=0, delta(5)=1, delta(10)=5 (Calhoun M(10)=50), delta(16)>=1 (M(16)>=121) - i.e. the best known lower bounds on tree deficiency are O(1) while the ruler deficiency is Theta(scope). The 6-vertex tree B_{2,2} tiles [1,15] perfectly - the exact feat impossible for 6-mark rulers - which pinpoints WHERE bushiness defeats the classical machinery. Consequently 'no Leech tree for n > n0' is equivalent to 'delta(n) >= 1 for n > 6', and any superconstant lower bound on delta(n) would be the first genuinely new asymptotic obstruction.
claims.proof_sketch: The equivalence is immediate: M(n) >= C(n,2) always (C(n,2) distinct positive distances); equality iff the distance set is exactly [1, C(n,2)]. The mechanism diagnosis (Sidon deficiency powers t>=6, trees have tiny known deficiency) is proved for the ruler side (Lindstroem/Sidon: G(m) >= m^2 - O(m^{3/2})) and observed for the tree side (Calhoun's Table 1 values, repo ledger L15); the claim that no OTHER mechanism hides in the classical proofs is my reading of the modern statements, not a verified reading of the 1978 proof (primary text inaccessible) - flag accordingly.
claims.checkable_prediction: delta is computable: extending Calhoun's M(n) table (n = 11..17 currently only lower-bounded) with the repo's forced-forest engine 'with gaps allowed' would test the key dichotomy: does delta(n) stay O(1) (PSDS mechanism truly dead for trees, SWZ finiteness needs a new idea) or grow (a threshold theorem for trees is plausible)? Even delta(11), delta(12) exactly would be informative and are within reach of the existing C++ engine.

claims.name: S1. Tree analog of 'petites composantes' / almost-covering threshold (proposed theorem target)
claims.statement: SPECULATIVE TARGET, precisely posed: call a family of vertex-disjoint edge-weighted trees T_1,...,T_m a distance-forest packing of [1,U] if all within-component distances are distinct and lie in [1,U]; let Q_s(U) = max coverage when every component has >= s vertices. Conjectured tree analogs: (a) (KT-1980 analog) every perfect distance forest (exact tiling of [1,S]) contains a component with fewer than s0 vertices, for some absolute s0; (b) (2608.13739 analog) Q_s(U) = U - Omega_s(U) for s >= s0. Status of evidence: FOR - the forced-forest cascade (repo L4/Calhoun Alg 2.7) shows every Leech tree's initial segments are exactly-tiled by its light-edge forest, so (a) with quantitative form would constrain ALL orders at once, and rulers (the extreme tree) have threshold 5/6; AGAINST - B_{2,2} shows single 6-vertex components tile perfectly, and bushy components have far more pairs per edge (C(e+1,2) vs e for the interval-crowding count), so s0, if it exists, is > 6 and the ruler proof does not transfer. NOTE the direction of application: (a)/(b) would NOT directly kill a single huge Leech tree (one component); they would kill the scattered-small-weights regimes and, combined with A3 (connectivity) and A4 (ladder), squeeze the forced-forest search from both sides at every order.
claims.proof_sketch: No proof; the posed statements are the exact transplants of Kotzig-Turgeon Ann. Discrete Math. 8 (1980) and arXiv:2608.13739 Thm 1.1 with 'ruler' replaced by 'distinct-distance tree'. A first attackable toy case: can m disjoint 6-vertex distinct-distance trees exactly tile [1, 15m] for some m >= 2? (m=1: yes, B_{2,2}.) This is finite for each m and CP-SAT-able for m = 2, 3 with the repo's machinery.
claims.checkable_prediction: The m=2 toy case (two 6-vertex tree components tiling [1,30]) is decidable in minutes with the repo's forced-forest engine run on 2-component forests with gaps disallowed; a nonexistence there would be the first data point for s0 <= 6 in the family setting despite B_{2,2}.

The cross-branch SUM structure (the repo's key structural fact at a vertex/centroid) is a 'sum-and-distance system' in the sense of Huxley-Lettington-Schmidt (Period. Math. best_route: Two-track recommendation. IMMEDIATE (deployable now, all proved, machine-checked): add to the constraint pack, at every order including 25+, (i) the component-refined forcing inequality w_{k+1} <= 1 + sum_i C(e_i+1,2) over the current forced forest (claim A2 - strictly finer than Calhoun whenever the forest is disconnected, and attained with equality inside known Leech trees, so it is the exact form); (ii) the connectivity trigger w_{k+1} >= C(k,2)+3 => the k lightest edges are connected (A3); (iii) the rigidity ladder w_q <= C(q,2) for q in {5,7,...,24} plus the branching anchors 'w_6 = 16 iff F_5 = B_{2,2}(1,2,5;4,8)' and 'w_4 = 7 iff F_3 = K_{1,3}(1,2,4)' (A4) - these convert every past and future order exclusion into a permanent -1 domain cut for all larger orders. THEORY TRACK (the PSDS-native route to 'no Leech trees for n > n0'): the import analysis shows the classical interval-tiling machinery is vacuous at threshold 1 (A1) and blind to the sum-holes (A0), so the transferable asset is the k >= 6 / almost-covering-threshold MECHANISM, not the theorems. The concrete program: (1) obtain the actual gap proofs (KT 1980 and arXiv:2608.13739) - see open questions; (2) prove the tree analog with components measured in vertices (claim S1), starting from the finite toy case 'two disjoint 6-vertex distinct-distance trees cannot tile [1,30]' (CP-SAT-able this week with existing code); (3) in parallel, compute exact tree-Golomb deficiencies delta(11), delta(12) (A7) to decide empirically whether delta(n) grows - if it does, a threshold theorem for perfect distance forests plus the forced-forest cascade (every Leech tree exactly tiles its initial segments with its light-edge forest at every scale) is a coherent, quantifier-clean route to nonexistence for large structured families, and it composes with the repo's centroid sum-side attack (which is exactly what the difference-side literature cannot see).

summary: Literature reconnaissance for importable nonexistence machinery for Leech trees (target: extend /Users/geoclaw/Documents/claude/projects/leech-trees/docs/literature-ledger.md). Main verdicts. (1) The perfect-systems-of-difference-sets (PSDS) literature is the closest proven analogue of the whole problem: a PSDS with threshold 1 is exactly a perfect distance forest whose components are paths, and there the field PROVED the full program we want — Bermond-Kotzig-Turgeon 1978: no perfect system whose components all have >= 6 elements (any number of components, any threshold); Abrham-Kotzig 1984: every perfect system with threshold c has >= c components of size <= 4 and average component size <= 6. The single-component case (perfect ruler <= 4 marks, Golomb 1972 = K_n graceful iff n<=4) is the path-Leech theorem; the tree-component generalization of the AK84 average-size bound IS "no Leech tree for n > n0". (2) A brand-new preprint (Ma-Yi, arXiv:2608.13739, Aug 2026) upgrades this to a quantitative covering-defect theorem: disjoint difference sets of t-mark Golomb rulers can cover 1-o(1) of an interval iff 3<=t<=5, and for t>=6 a positive-density gap >= ((t-1)*0.43447-2)/(2(t-2)) (2.15% at t=6) is forced, by a one-frequency Fourier obstruction — the same constant gamma_0 = d*-2 from the Redei-Renyi/Leech/Bernshteyn-Tait difference-basis defect d* in [2.4345, 2.6458]. This is the model theorem and the model technique for a "tree covering defect". (3) Downstream Leech literature: the only asymptotic progress since SWZ 2005 is Luo-Yu (Involve 17 (2024) 327-335): no diameter-3 Leech tree of order >= 7, at most finitely many diameter-4 Leech trees, and (via Cilleruelo's equidistribution of dense Sidon sets) the new bound sum over DISTINCT vertex degrees d_i^2 <= (1/4+o(1)) n^2 — strictly better than SWZ Thm 3 and than the repo's 0.7n star-Sidon asymptotic. Also discovered: a published one-page ERRATUM to SWZ 2005 (Bull. ICA 52 (2008), p. 6, Zbl 1145.05305) — directly relevant to the repo's L9-UNCLEAR flag on SWZ Theorem 3 — and a pre-SWZ computer paper (Yang-Zhang-Ding, Ars Combin. 39 (1995) 249-254). Nobody in the citation graph attempts general nonexistence. (4) Sidon toolbox with best constants assembled (Erdos-Turan 1941, Lindstrom 1969, Balogh-Furedi-Roy 2023 sqrt(n)+0.998 n^{1/4}; B_2[g]: Cilleruelo-Ruzsa-Trujillo 1.864 sqrt(gN), Martin-O'Bryant/Yu sqrt(min(3.1694g, 1.74217(2g-1)) N), Habsieger-Plagne 2018; Cilleruelo 2000 gap/equidistribution theorem). For "half-Sidon" (cross-branch-only) nothing off-the-shelf exists; nearest concepts are weak Sidon sets (Ma-Tang arXiv:2602.23282) and graph sum index (wrong optimization direction); modern higher-energy methods (Shkredov, Combinatorica 2023) are candidate machinery. (5) Modular Leech trees exist at order 8 (Leach 2014) — proof that counting/parity arguments alone cannot yield nonexistence; any proof must use the integer-interval (archimedean) structure, exactly as in the Fourier-defect theorems. Difference-triangle-set LP bounds (Kloeve 1988/89, Lorentzen-Nilsen 1991, Shearer ELJC 1999: M(I,5) >= (91I+6)/6, M(5,5)=79, plus the cheap averaging Lemma m >= r+(n-1)/2) are the packing-side lower-bound tools, directly addable to the repo's relaxations though numerically non-binding at n=18. Full texts archived in the scratchpad (dts_lp.txt, gs80.txt, diffbase.txt, bkg.txt).

claims.name: Bermond-Kotzig-Turgeon 1978 (Colloq. Math. Soc. Janos Bolyai 18, 135-149, 'On a combinatorial problem of antennas in radioastronomy')
claims.statement: An (m,{k_1..k_m},c)-PSDS is a family of m integer sets ('components', sizes k_i) whose internal positive differences collectively hit every element of {c, c+1, ..., c-1+SUM C(k_i,2)} exactly once. Theorem: no (m,k,c)-PSDS exists for ANY m >= 1, c >= 1 when k >= 6 (all components of size >= 6 impossible). For k = 5: m >= 4c necessary; for k = 3,4: m >= 2c-1 plus congruence conditions m mod 4.
claims.proof_sketch: Verbatim from the survey arXiv:2510.20446 (Prop 1.1/1.2, fetched twice, consistent). Technique: differences of a component form a difference triangle; every non-top-row entry is a sum of >= 2 top-row entries, hence >= 2c, so the c integers in [c,2c) must all be top-row (adjacent) differences; combined with the exact total-sum identity SUM(differences) = Dc + D(D-1)/2 (D = total count) and per-triangle weighted-sum bounds (each top gap g_i is counted i(k-i) times) large components overshoot. This is literally the path-forest case of the repo's cut identity.
claims.checkable_prediction: A perfect distance forest with threshold 1 whose components are all paths must contain a path component with <= 5 vertices; verifiable against any path-only states enumerated by the repo's forced-forest engine (src/, data/trees_*.jsonl checks).

claims.name: Abrham-Kotzig 1984, 'Inequalities for perfect systems of difference sets', Discrete Math. 50 (Zbl 0554.05013); with Kotzig-Turgeon 1980 'Sur l'existence de petites composantes...', Ann. Discrete Math. 8, 71-75 (Zbl 0464.05011) and Abrham 1982 'Bounds for the sizes of components...', Ann. Discrete Math. 12, 1-7 (Zbl 0492.05011)
claims.statement: Every perfect system of difference sets starting with c >= 1 contains at least c components of size <= 4, and the AVERAGE size of the components is <= 6 (quoted verbatim from the zbMATH review of Zbl 0554.05013). KT 1980 is the earlier qualitative small-components theorem; Abrham 1982 has further size bounds (texts paywalled, statements not retrieved).
claims.proof_sketch: Statement from the zbMATH Open review (reviews of the two Annals-of-Discrete-Math papers are license-blocked; primary texts behind ScienceDirect 403). Technique per the survey literature: dyadic counting of small differences (rows of the difference triangles) against the exact-cover requirement. At threshold c=1 (the Leech-relevant case): at least one component with <= 4 elements, average <= 6.
claims.checkable_prediction: The single-component case forces size <= 4 = the perfect-ruler theorem. A tree-component analogue of 'average component size <= 6' applied to a 1-component system would give n <= n0 for perfect distance TREES, i.e. exactly the goal statement; any proof attempt should first reproduce AK84 for paths as a sanity check.

claims.name: Golomb 1972, 'How to number a graph' (in Graph Theory and Computing, Academic Press, 23-37); equivalently no perfect ruler with >= 5 marks
claims.statement: A perfect Golomb ruler (m marks, all C(m,2) differences distinct AND exactly {1,...,C(m,2)}) exists only for m <= 4 ({0,1}, {0,1,3}, {0,1,4,6}). Equivalently K_m is graceful iff m <= 4. This is the path case of the Leech problem (repo L3) and the single-component case of the BKT/AK84 theorems (a (1,m,1)-PSDS).
claims.proof_sketch: Standard citation per MathWorld (Golomb 1972; Gardner 1983 p.154); also follows from PSDS Prop 1.2: k=5 needs m >= 4c = 4 components, k >= 6 impossible outright. The repo has its own re-derivation (ledger L3); the graceful-K_n guise is the standard reference to cite in the paper draft.
claims.checkable_prediction: None new; anchors the citation chain (Leech 1975 -> Golomb 1972 -> PSDS).

claims.name: Ma-Yi 2026, 'An Almost-Covering Threshold for Golomb-Ruler Difference Packings', arXiv:2608.13739 (Aug 2026)
claims.statement: Let P_t(U) = max total coverage of [1,U] by pairwise disjoint difference sets of t-mark Golomb rulers. Then P_t(U) = U - o(U) iff 3 <= t <= 5; for t >= 6, liminf_{U->inf} (1 - P_t(U)/U) >= ((t-1)*gamma_0 - 2)/(2(t-2)) with gamma_0 = 0.4344672564... (= d* - 2, the Leech difference-basis constant); at t = 6 the forced uncovered fraction is >= 2.15%.
claims.proof_sketch: From the arXiv abstract (small-model fetch; exact constant and iff-threshold quoted). Techniques named: existence spectra of perfect difference families (t=3,4), Wild's product construction (t=5), a one-frequency Fourier obstruction, and discrete small-difference bounds (t >= 14). This is the quantitative, positive-density upgrade of BKT k>=6 and the exact template for a 'tree covering defect' theorem.
claims.checkable_prediction: 2.15% defect at t=6 must be consistent with Shearer's DTS tables and with the repo's Golomb data; numerically checkable. If the one-frequency Fourier obstruction extends to systems mixing within-branch differences and cross-branch sums, it directly attacks spiders and double brooms — the exact open middle regime at large n.

claims.name: Redei-Renyi 1949 + Leech 1956 + Golay 1972 + Bernshteyn-Tait 2019 (arXiv:1901.09411, full text verified): the difference-basis covering defect
claims.statement: D(n) = min size of A with A-A containing [1,n]. Then d* = lim D(n)^2/n exists (RR49) and 2.4344...+eps <= d* <= 2.6458...: lower bounds 2+4/(3pi) = 2.4244 (RR49), 2 - 2 inf_{theta<>0} sin(theta)/theta = 2.4344 (Leech 1956), strictly improved by eps ~ 10^-3 (Bernshteyn-Tait 2019, Fourier-analytic); upper bounds 2.6646 (Leech), 2.6458 (Golay 1972). Since d* > 2 strictly, covering an interval by differences costs a permanent >= 10% overhead in marks over the packing count — perfect covering is impossible even asymptotically in 1D.
claims.proof_sketch: Full text read (diffbase.txt in scratchpad). Lower-bound technique: the uniform measure pushed to the circle must have first (RR/Leech) resp. higher (B-T) Fourier coefficients compatible with A-A covering [1,n]; an autocorrelation-positivity obstruction. Consequence recorded in Graham-Sloane 1980 (16): lim g(v)/v^2 = 1/d* <= 0.411 for the largest graceful graph on v nodes — the model 'labeling dies of a covering-defect' statement.
claims.checkable_prediction: Only the path/caterpillar-spine parts of a tree are 1-D embeddable, so this applies verbatim only to paths; the checkable analogue: any claimed tree-defect proof must reduce to (and not contradict) d* in [2.435, 2.646] in the path case.

claims.name: Kloeve 1988/1989 (IEEE Trans. IT 34, 355-361 and 35, 879-886) + Lorentzen-Nilsen 1991 + Shearer 1999 (Electron. J. Combin. 6, #R31, full text verified): difference triangle set lower bounds
claims.statement: (I,J)-DTS: I rulers of J+1 marks each, ALL I*J(J+1)/2 differences distinct; M(I,J) = min possible largest difference. LP lower bounds from: (i) any k distinct positive integers sum to >= k(k+1)/2 applied to every subset of the differences; (ii) Shearer's averaging lemma: n distinct integers with average r have max >= r + (n-1)/2, applied to every top set. Exact yields: M(I,5) >= (91I+6)/6, M(I,6) >= (179I+9)/8, M(5,5) = 79 (Kloeve's published 83 is WRONG - corrected by exhaustive search), M(2,9) = 121, M(3,7) = 100, M(9,4) = 91.
claims.proof_sketch: Full text read (dts_lp.txt in scratchpad). Any family of vertex-disjoint paths in a Leech tree with J edges each is an (I,J)-DTS with scope <= N, so N >= M(I,J). Numerically non-binding at n=18 (M grows linearly in I, N quadratically in n), but inequality family (ii) is a strictly stronger, essentially free addition to the repo's LP/QP relaxations (theory-notes F3/F4).
claims.checkable_prediction: Adding Shearer-type (subset-average) inequalities to the repo's majorization QP should kill strictly more topologies than the current F3/F4 (which only use inequality family (i)); testable on data/trees_18.jsonl.

claims.name: Sidon sets in [1,n], best constants: Erdos-Turan 1941 (J. London Math. Soc. 16, 212-215), Lindstrom 1969 (J. Combin. Theory 6, 211-212), Balogh-Furedi-Roy 2023 (Amer. Math. Monthly 130(5), 437-445; arXiv:2103.15850)
claims.statement: F(n) = max size of a Sidon subset of [1,n] satisfies F(n) <= n^{1/2} + O(n^{1/4}) (ET41), F(n) < n^{1/2} + n^{1/4} + 1 (Lindstrom), and F(n) <= n^{1/2} + 0.998 n^{1/4} for n large (BFR 2023 - first error-term improvement in 50+ years); lower bound (1-o(1)) n^{1/2} (Singer 1938). Erdos's $500 problem F(n) = n^{1/2} + o(n^{1/4}) remains open. Inverted: a Golomb ruler with m marks has length >= m^2 - 2*0.998 m^{3/2}(1+o(1)).
claims.proof_sketch: Standard; BFR constant confirmed from two independent sources (paper record + Johnston-Tait-Timmons intro, bkg.txt). Technique: windowed count of differences (ET41) refined by counting collisions of translates (BFR). These are the quantitative inputs behind the repo's F1 (Golomb diameter) at large n.
claims.checkable_prediction: Gives explicit asymptotic G(m) >= m^2 - 1.996 m^{3/2}(1+o(1)), consistent with OEIS A003022 values used in ledger L6.

claims.name: Cilleruelo 2000, 'Gaps in dense Sidon sets', Integers 0, #A11 (free PDF: math.colgate.edu/~integers/a11/a11.pdf) - the equidistribution engine behind Luo-Yu
claims.statement: If A subset [1,N] is Sidon with |A| = N^{1/2} - L, then every interval I of length cN contains c|A| + E_I elements with |E_I| <= 52 N^{1/4} (1 + c^{1/2} N^{1/8})(1 + L^{1/2}). Corollary: |A| = N^{1/2} + O(N^{1/4}) implies max gap g(A) << N^{3/4}, and the exponent 3/4 is best possible.
claims.proof_sketch: Statement quoted from the paper via search capture; the free PDF should be archived into docs/sources/. Technique: Fourier/second-moment count of differences in short windows. Near-maximal Sidon sets are forced to be equidistributed — so a Leech-tree star whose incident weights form a near-extremal weak Sidon set has weights spread through [1,N], which then collides with the containment bound d(x,y) <= N+1-s_x s_y and the cut identity.
claims.checkable_prediction: The n=18 star-Sidon witness {1,2,4,7,12,23,32,41,56,70,83} (ledger L11) has all elements <= 83 = far from equidistributed in [1,153]; Cilleruelo's theorem quantifies why such witnesses stop existing as d approaches the extremal size at large n.

claims.name: Luo-Yu 2024, 'A graph labeling problem', Involve 17(2), 327-335, doi:10.2140/involve.2024.17.327 (statements from Froncek's zbMATH review Zbl 1544.05094; full text paywalled)
claims.statement: (i) No Leech star of order > 4 and no diameter-3 Leech tree with more than 6 vertices; (ii) there are at most FINITELY MANY diameter-4 Leech trees; (iii) if d_1, ..., d_k are the DISTINCT vertex degrees of a Leech tree of order n then d_1^2 + d_2^2 + ... + d_k^2 <= (1/4 + o(1)) n^2. In particular Delta <= (1/2 + o(1)) n, improving SWZ Thm 3's claimed (3/8)^{1/2} n = 0.612n and the repo's 0.7n star-Sidon asymptotic; and two vertices of distinct near-maximal degrees are excluded simultaneously.

Result (ii) is remarkable because Calhoun 2007 Fig. 11 shows the forced-forest search tree for diameter 4 is infinite - Luo-Yu must have a genuinely different finiteness argument; obtaining it is a priority.
claims.checkable_prediction: At n=18 the asymptotic form is not directly usable (o(1) unquantified), but the METHOD (equidistribution + containment) should reprove the repo's exact Delta <= 11 and plausibly Delta <= 10; a finite-n version of their Lemma chain is a concrete strengthening target.

claims.name: Route synthesis (this session): what a provable general-nonexistence theorem should look like

Trivially T(n) <= C(n,2); Leech trees exist for infinitely many n only if T(n) = C(n,2) infinitely often. CONJECTURED ROUTE: T(n) <= (1-delta) C(n,2) for some absolute delta > 0 and all n >= n0. summary: Two-ended covering rigidity delivered three kinds of results. (1) SMALL END, exact: the forcing lemma localizes to the Kruskal merge profile — running edges in weight order with merge products a_k*b_k (which sum to exactly N), the schedule w_{k+1} <= 1 + sum_{j<=k} a_j b_j holds for every k, refines Calhoun's bound by the component count of the light forest (each extra component lowers the ceiling), and yields an exact 'waste identity' sum_k w_k a_k b_k = N(N+1)/2 - TotalWaste plus the new inequality TotalWaste >= (sum_k (a_k b_k)^2 - N)/2, so a balanced heaviest cut forces ~n^4/32 waste (long-hop pairs). (2) TOP END, new and the headline: (a) crowding — any family of pairwise disjoint pairs with distance >= N-q has size <= sqrt(2q+1) (generalizes Lemma 4a; proved via the 4-point condition, 62,856 random-tree quadruples checked), so all far pairs are covered by <= 2*sqrt(2q+1) 'poles'; (b) WINDOW THEOREMS — the values above the largest 'non-cross' distance D_2 must be tiled exactly by a sumset of two deficit sets whose internal structure is forced (pendant weights at a pole: distinct pairwise sums; path-tail distances: distinct differences); exhaustive finite searches, independently double-implemented, prove the window N - D_2 is at most 10 for every Leech double broom, at most 7 for every broom-with-path-handle, and exactly ell_2 - ell_3 in {1,2,4,5} for every Leech spider with >= 3 legs, AT EVERY ORDER n. Consequences: balanced double brooms (both max pendant weights >= 11) do not exist; a broom on a handle has max pendant weight <= 7 (hence <= 4 leaves); every spider's 2nd and 3rd deepest legs differ by <= 5 while ell_1 + ell_2 = N. These are the first order-independent structural family exclusions beyond stars and paths. (3) MIDDLE: the surviving family is precisely pinned — few-pole trees whose two deepest arms are 'thick' (must branch within weighted distance ~10 of their deep ends, since bare-path and bare-broom tips are capped), with hop-diameter <= sqrt(N)+N^{1/4}+1, max degree <~ sqrt(N), L >= 3; spiders/brooms saturate the crowding bound exactly, which is why counting alone stalls and the window tilings are the right new tool. All claims machine-checked against the five known Leech trees (all pass; known trees sit tight against the small-end schedule at almost every step). claims.name: Kruskal covering schedule
claims.statement: Let T be a Leech tree of order n, N=C(n,2), weights w_1<...<w_{n-1}. Process edges in increasing weight (Kruskal); the k-th edge merges components of sizes a_k, b_k; let Pi_k = sum_{j<=k} a_j b_j (= number of pairs spanned by the forest F_k of the k lightest edges). Then (i) sum_{k=1}^{n-1} a_k b_k = N exactly; (ii) for every k in {0,...,n-2}: w_{k+1} <= 1 + Pi_k, with deficit exactly sigma_k = #{pairs inside F_k with distance > w_{k+1}} (so w_{k+1} = 1 + Pi_k - sigma_k); (iii) k = n-2 recovers the containment bound w_{n-1} <= N+1-s(n-s) for the heaviest edge, unifying the small end and the heaviest-edge squeeze in one schedule.
claims.proof_sketch: By the forcing lemma, F_k realizes every value 1..w_{k+1}-1 (a pair of value < w_{k+1} uses only lighter edges, hence lies in F_k) and cannot realize w_{k+1} (the (k+1)-st edge does; distances are distinct). The number of realized values is at most the number of pairs spanned, Pi_k, and the pairs spanned by a growing forest are counted exactly by the merge products. Verified exactly on all five known Leech trees (check_rigidity.py).
claims.checkable_prediction: For any weighted-forest search node, prune when the forced next weight exceeds 1 + (pairs spanned). Empirically the five known trees satisfy w_{k+1} = 1 + Pi_k with EQUALITY at every step except the final step of L6 (w_5 = 8 < 11): zero small-end waste.

claims.name: Component concentration bound
claims.statement: With m_k = number of nontrivial components of the light forest F_k: w_{k+1} <= C(k - m_k + 2, 2) + m_k for every k. The case m_k = 1 is Calhoun's w_{k+1} <= C(k+1,2)+1; every additional component strictly lowers the ceiling (by ~(k-m_k)). Contrapositive: weight growth near the Calhoun ceiling forces the light forest to be a single subtree ('cluster'). This answers the small-end structural question: the light forest need not be a subtree in general (L4_path and L6 have steps with m_k = 2, and both sit exactly AT this bound), but concentration is forced exactly to the extent that weights grow fast.
claims.proof_sketch: F_k realizes all of 1..w_{k+1}-1, so w_{k+1}-1 <= sum_i C(v_i,2) over component sizes v_i with sum(v_i - 1) = k. By convexity the maximum over m parts is attained at sizes (k-m+2, 2, ..., 2), giving C(k-m+2,2) + (m-1) + 1 after adding 1. Checked on all five known trees; L4_path step 2 and L6 step 3 are tight with m=2 (check_rigidity.py).
claims.checkable_prediction: In topology-aware weight searches, the bound kills branches where small weights are forced onto vertex-disjoint edges while the forced value grows quadratically.

claims.name: Waste identity and waste-merge inequality
claims.statement: Define Pi(t) = #pairs spanned by edges of weight <= t and TotalWaste TW = sum_{t=1}^{N} (Pi(t) - t) (each summand >= 0 by covering). Then EXACTLY: TW = N(N+1)/2 - sum_k w_k a_k b_k = sum over pairs P with hop >= 2 of (d_P - M_P), where M_P is the largest weight on P's path. Moreover TW >= (sum_k (a_k b_k)^2 - N)/2. Consequence: if the heaviest cut is balanced (a_{n-1}b_{n-1} = s(n-s) ~ n^2/4) then TW >~ n^4/32, i.e. a quarter-ish of the total moment N(N+1)/2 must consist of pairs whose distance greatly exceeds the largest weight on their path — forcing many long-hop pairs, which fights bushiness. This makes precise where the cut identity's slack lives.
claims.proof_sketch: A pair P contributes to Pi(t)-t for exactly t in [M_P, d_P), giving the double-counting identity; sum_P M_P = sum_k w_k a_k b_k since the pairs first spanned at step k have path-max w_k. The inequality: substitute w_k <= 1 + Pi_{k-1} into sum w_k (Pi_k - Pi_{k-1}) and use sum Pi_{k-1} dPi = (N^2 - sum dPi^2)/2. Verified on L6: TW = 41 >= (67-15)/2 = 26 (check_rigidity.py).
claims.checkable_prediction: For any candidate n=25 topology with a central heaviest edge (s ~ 12), at least (s(n-s))^2/2 - N/2 units of waste must be scheduled; topologies too bushy to supply long-hop pairs are infeasible — implementable as a filter.

claims.name: Far-pair crowding (generalizes Lemma 4a)
claims.statement: In a Leech tree, for every q with 1 <= q <= (N-1)/2: every family of PAIRWISE DISJOINT pairs, each with distance >= N - q, has size k <= sqrt(2q+1). (q=1: the pairs realizing N and N-1 intersect = Lemma 4a.)
claims.proof_sketch: For two disjoint far pairs {x,y},{x',y'}, the tree four-point condition (two largest of the three pairing sums are equal) forces at least two of the four cross distances to be >= N-2q: if the sum d(x,y)+d(x',y') is maximal, the tied partner sum >= 2(N-q) has both terms <= N hence both >= N-2q; otherwise both cross sums strictly exceed 2(N-q) and all four cross distances are >= N-2q+1. Cross pairs from different index pairs are distinct vertex pairs (disjointness), and distinct from the k original pairs, so k + 2*C(k,2) = k^2 distinct pairs carry distinct values in the window [N-2q, N] of size 2q+1. Machine check: the cross-distance lemma tested on 62,856 quadruples in 300 random distinct-distance trees, 0 failures (check_rigidity.py).
claims.checkable_prediction: In any exhaustive run at an admissible order, no candidate assignment can place 3 pairwise disjoint pairs among the top 4 values, 4 disjoint among the top 8, etc.

claims.name: Pole cover of the top window
claims.statement: For every q <= (N-1)/2 there is a vertex set X_q with |X_q| <= 2*sqrt(2q+1) meeting every pair of distance > N - q. Hence the top q values of a Leech tree live on O(sqrt(q)) 'poles'. Taking q ~ n: the top ~n values are carried by O(sqrt(n)) vertices. Tightness: two long arms with ~sqrt(2q) deep vertices each (double brooms, spiders) saturate the bound exactly — so this counting is best possible and identifies the extremal middle family; further progress must use the VALUES (window tiling), not just counts.
claims.proof_sketch: Take both endpoints of a maximal matching of the far-pair graph; by the crowding claim the matching has size <= sqrt(2q+1); every far pair meets it by maximality.
claims.checkable_prediction: In any Leech tree of order 25, the 25 pairs realizing values >= N-24 are covered by at most 2*sqrt(49) = 14 vertices.

claims.name: Largest-weight lower bound
claims.statement: w_{n-1} >= N/h + (h-1)/2 where h is the hop length of the value-N path; minimizing over h, w_{n-1} >= sqrt(2N) - 1/2 (approximately n - 1/2) for every Leech tree. Two-sided squeeze with containment: sqrt(2N) - 1/2 <= w_{n-1} <= N + 1 - s(n-s), and by the covering schedule the upper-bound deficit is exactly the number of within-side pairs exceeding w_{n-1}. (Repo previously had only upper bounds on the max weight.)
claims.proof_sketch: The value-N path carries h distinct positive weights summing to N; h distinct positive integers with maximum W sum to at most hW - h(h-1)/2, so N <= h*w_max - C(h,2). The function N/h + (h-1)/2 is minimized at h = sqrt(2N). Verified on all five known trees (L6: w_max = 8 >= 4.98).
claims.checkable_prediction: Any order-25 Leech tree has an edge of weight >= ceil(sqrt(600) - 0.5) = 24; order-36: >= 35.

claims.name: Centroid reformulation of containment; leaf-count status
claims.statement: Root T at a centroid c. For every Q < n/2, the pairs with s_x s_y <= Q are EXACTLY the pairs (x,y) of non-root vertices, incomparable in the rooted order, with |subtree(x)|*|subtree(y)| <= Q; and Leech requires at least Q such pairs for every Q (the top Q values need them, distinct). Negative result recorded honestly: this counting CANNOT force a growing leaf bound — a bare path already satisfies it for all Q (its two end segments supply a vertex of every small subtree size), so combs/caterpillars pass; the true leaf bound remains L >= 3 for n >= 5, which follows because L = 2 means the tree is a path, i.e. a perfect difference basis (perfect ruler), impossible for >= 5 marks (classical; cf. SWZ's no-Leech-paths).
claims.proof_sketch: For Q < n/2 both sides s_x, s_y <= Q < n/2, so the first path edge at x points into x's unique giant branch, which in the centroid rooting is the parent side; then s_x = |subtree(x)|, and y outside subtree(x) (and symmetrically) is exactly incomparability. Machine-checked as set equality for all Q < n/2 on all five known trees (check_rigidity.py). The L >= 3 part is literature (no perfect rulers with >= 5 marks).
claims.checkable_prediction: Filter for topology lists: for each Q < n/2, count incomparable centroid-subtree-product-<= Q pairs; require >= Q. Strictly refines the repo's F5 (degree form), since s_x = subtree size >= degree.

claims.name: Double-broom window theorem (order-independent family exclusion)
claims.statement: Let T be any Leech double broom (two poles v_A, v_B joined by a path of weighted length P; all other vertices are pendant leaves at the poles, with pendant weight sets B^A, B^B; N = maxB^A + P + maxB^B). Let D_2 = the largest distance among pairs that are NOT (A-leaf, B-leaf) cross pairs. Then N - D_2 <= 10 (and N - D_2 != 8). Equivalently: EITHER min(max B^A, max B^B) <= 10, OR one broom has two pendant weights summing to >= N - 10 (a degenerate shape whose diameter lies inside a single broom). Corollary: in the first case the short side's pendant weights lie in [1,10] and are pairwise-sum-distinct, so that broom has at most 5 leaves (max weak-Sidon subset of [1,10] has size 5). Hence BALANCED double brooms — both maximum pendant weights >= 11 and no intra-broom near-spanning pair — exist at NO order n. This is the first structural family exclusion beyond stars and paths that is uniform in n; consistent with L6 (window = 2, min-side max pendant = 2).
claims.proof_sketch: Machine-assisted but fully rigorous. Values in (D_2, N] (a window of M = N - D_2 consecutive values) are realized exactly once each and only by cross pairs, whose value is N - (alpha_i + beta_j) with deficit sets alpha = maxB^A - B^A (containing 0), beta likewise. So alpha (+) beta covers [0, M) exactly once; all cross sums are globally distinct (distinct distances); alpha and beta each have all pairwise sums distinct, because b_i + b_j is the distance between two leaves of the same pole (weak Sidon). If M >= 11, restrict both sets to [0, 11): all constraints are inherited by subsets, and covering [0,11) uses only elements < 11 — but exhaustive enumeration of ALL pairs of weak-Sidon subsets of {0,...,10} containing 0 shows no pair covers [0,11) exactly with globally distinct cross sums (verified by two independent implementations: DFS in tiling_search.py/tiling_search3.py and full subset enumeration in independent_verify.py; the DFS additionally shows every M in {8} u [11, 200] individually infeasible under the full constraint set including (alpha-alpha) cap (beta-beta) = {0} and the no-deficit-equals-M constraint, both also proved necessary). Windows M <= 7 and M in {9,10} are combinatorially feasible (e.g. alpha={0,3,6}, beta={0,1,2,9} tiles [0,10)), so 10 is sharp for this constraint set.
claims.checkable_prediction: No Leech tree at any admissible order (25, 27, 36, ...) is a double broom with both maximum pendant weights >= 11 unless one broom internally spans >= N - 10; finite per-order checks of the surviving degenerate cases become trivial. Also explains why the ledger's B_{8,4} double-star sub-shape search was hard but the full-tree question is easy: full Leech surjectivity is what forces the tiling.

claims.name: Spider window theorem: second and third legs nearly tie
claims.statement: Let T be any Leech spider (all legs are paths from a single center) with p >= 3 legs of weighted lengths ell_1 > ell_2 > ell_3 > ... (distinct automatically). Then N = ell_1 + ell_2 and ell_2 - ell_3 is in {1, 2, 4, 5}; in particular ell_2 - ell_3 <= 5, at EVERY order n. So every Leech spider has one dominant leg (ell_1 = N - ell_2) and a near-tie between the 2nd and 3rd deepest legs. Consistent with L4_star (legs 4 > 2 > 1: gap 1).
claims.proof_sketch: Same window machinery with Golomb replacing weak Sidon: the window (ell_1 + ell_3, N] of M = ell_2 - ell_3 values is covered exactly by leg1 x leg2 pairs, d(x,y) = d_c(x) + d_c(y), with deficits alpha_x = d(leaf_1, x), beta_y = d(leaf_2, y); differences within each deficit set are within-leg distances (collinear), hence all distinct (Golomb), and the two legs' difference sets are disjoint except 0 (global distance distinctness). Exhaustive enumeration (both implementations) shows two Golomb sets containing 0 cannot cover [0, K) exactly with globally distinct cross sums for any K >= 6 (prefix infeasible at K = 6..13 checked; restriction monotonicity extends to all K), and the full-constraint DFS shows M = 3 is also infeasible while M in {2,4,5} are feasible; M = 1 trivially feasible. Weak-Sidon/Golomb ablation confirms the internal structure constraint is what caps the window (without it, every M is feasible via de Bruijn digit tilings).
claims.checkable_prediction: Any spider topology at n = 25 whose real-relaxation forces ell_2 - ell_3 >= 6 (e.g. via per-leg Golomb-ruler length gaps: leg lengths are OGR-constrained, so hop-length differences of >= 2 between legs 2 and 3 often force ell_2 - ell_3 >= 6) can be killed without weight search.

claims.name: Mixed cap: broom against path; broom-with-handle trees
claims.statement: If the two deep arms carrying the top window are a pendant broom (weak-Sidon deficits) and a path tail (Golomb deficits), the window caps at 7: N - D_2 <= 7. Family consequence: a 'broom with a handle' (single broom at a pole plus one bare path arm, i.e. a star-like caterpillar end) satisfies max pendant weight <= 7 (so at most 4 leaves in the broom, the max weak-Sidon subset of [1,7]) OR has two pendants summing >= N - 7. Together with the double-broom and spider caps: bare-path tips and bare-broom tips are both forbidden at the two deep ends of any Leech tree unless the structure degenerates — the deep arms must branch ('thicken') within weighted distance ~10 of their extremes.
claims.proof_sketch: Same argument; exhaustive check shows weak-Sidon x Golomb exact covers of [0,K) with distinct cross sums are impossible for every K >= 8 (prefix infeasible K=8..15 + restriction monotonicity; feasible for M <= 7). The 'thickening' consequence for general trees is the contrapositive: if the vertices within weighted distance ~10 of both deep endpoints form a bare path or a pendant broom, the corresponding window cap applies verbatim, so D_2 >= N - 10 forces a near-diameter pair elsewhere (recursion/descent).
claims.checkable_prediction: Every surviving n=25/27 topology, once weighted, must place a branch vertex within weighted distance 10 of the deep end of BOTH arms realizing N, or realize one of the enumerated degenerate cases.

claims.name: Survivor family synthesis (where the missing lemma must bite)
claims.statement: A Leech tree of order n must satisfy simultaneously: hop-diameter D <= sqrt(N) + N^{1/4} + 1 ~ 0.71n (Golomb + Erdos-Turan; exact OGR tables per order), max degree Delta <= (1+o(1))sqrt(N) ~ 0.71n (star-Sidon), L >= 3 leaves, largest weight >= sqrt(2N) - 1/2, the Kruskal covering schedule at the small end, the crowding/pole-cover structure at the top (top q values on <= 2 sqrt(2q+1) poles, saturated by two-arm shapes), and the window caps (no bare-path or bare-broom pair of deep arms in balance). The surviving middle family is exactly: multi-pole trees whose >= 2 deep arms are thick (branch within ~10 of the tips) with second-tier arm reaches nearly tied, e.g. spiders-with-branching-tips having p ~ sqrt(n) arms whose windows are covered by unions of >= 3 deficit sumsets. The missing lemma is a cap for r-fold sumset unions of structured deficit sets (r >= 3), which would propagate the near-tie ell_2 ~ ell_3 down the whole arm hierarchy and collide with the vertex budget n.
claims.proof_sketch: Each listed constraint is separately proved (above and in repo Lemmas 3, 5); the synthesis and the identification of union-tiling as the open bottleneck follow from: (a) crowding is tight on two-arm shapes, so counting stalls; (b) two-arm windows are capped by the finite searches; (c) with r arms the window above the (r+1)-st reach is an exact cover by C(r,2)-many pairwise sumsets of Golomb/weak-Sidon sets sharing factors — a finite, searchable object for each r.
claims.checkable_prediction: The r=3 union-tiling search (cover [0,M) exactly by alpha(+)beta_2 union alpha(+)beta_3 union beta_2(+)beta_3-type shifted sumsets, all Golomb, shifts >= 1) has a finite cap M_3; if M_3 <= ~30 then every Leech spider satisfies ell_2 - ell_4 <= M_3, and iterating gives ell_2 - ell_p <= M_p with M_p polynomial, forcing all second-tier legs into a bounded-width band.

claims.name: Small-end tightness of known trees (empirical)
claims.statement: All five known Leech trees satisfy w_{k+1} = 1 + Pi_k (zero waste at the moment of forcing) at every Kruskal step except the single final step of L6. Speculative conjecture: Leech trees require small-end waste sigma_k = 0 (equivalently w_{k+1} = 1 + Pi_k) for all k below some threshold growing with n; combined with the waste-merge inequality (which FORCES total waste ~n^4/32 when the heaviest cut is balanced) this would push the waste to late/large scales and might separate the small-end cluster from the heavy-cut structure.
claims.proof_sketch: Observation machine-verified (check_rigidity.py). No proof mechanism yet: sigma_k = 0 says every pair spanned early realizes a small value, i.e. the light cluster is 'perfect' as a distance set; plausibly provable for the first few k via case analysis (w_1=1, w_2=2 known; w_3 in {3,4} known), open beyond.
claims.checkable_prediction: If an order-25 Leech tree exists, its 4 lightest edges span pairs realizing exactly {1,...,Pi_4} with at most 1 exception; testable in any future search log.

open_questions: r-fold union tilings: what is the maximal M such that [0,M) can be covered exactly once by the union of the pairwise sumsets of r >= 3 deficit sets (each Golomb or weak-Sidon, pairwise difference-disjoint, all sums globally distinct, non-leading sets shifted by >= 1)? A finite search per r; a polynomial cap M_r would force all second-tier arm reaches of any Leech spider/multi-broom into a band of width M_p and likely kill all spiders at large n.

General deep-arm structure: when the deep ~10-neighborhood of an arm tip is a path-with-twigs or broom-with-stem (not bare), which subsets of the deficit set inherit Golomb/Sidon constraints, and is there still a finite window cap? (The ablation shows SOME internal constraint is needed: with none, de Bruijn digit tilings realize every window.)

Descent: N - D_2 <= 10 pushes a pair of distance >= N - 10 into a non-cross position; formalize the recursion (it lands inside one side or on a pole) and find the terminating contradiction against the pole-cover bound |X_q| <= 2 sqrt(2q+1) and the vertex budget.
Can the small-end tightness observation (w_{k+1} = 1 + Pi_k for small k) be proved for k <= K(n)? Even K = 5 would strongly constrain the light cluster's shape and interact with the component bound.

The KEY pendant fact ((A-A) cap (B-B) = {0}) was NOT needed for the window caps (ablation: weak-Sidon/Golomb alone suffices); where does it add power? Natural target: multi-sumset searches and the broom-side small-value cascade (it forces the weight-1 edge to be pendant at the broom containing the deficit-1 pair).

Quantify the caps' killing power on real topology lists: how many of the 122,344 n=18 survivors, and what fraction of n=25/27 topologies, are double brooms / spiders / broom-handles or have bare tips within distance 10 (killed outright by the caps)?

Is the window value N - D_2 = 8 exclusion (double brooms) and the {1,2,4,5} gap set (spiders) usable as a parity-like invariant elsewhere — i.e., do other two-arm families have punctured feasible windows?
best_route: The route that now looks provable: top-window exact tilings against arm-local structure, iterated. Concretely: (1) the window above the largest non-cross distance must be tiled EXACTLY by sumsets of deficit sets, and whenever a deficit set comes from a bare path tail (differences are distances: Golomb) or a pendant broom (sums are distances: weak Sidon) the window is capped by a finite, already-verified constant (5 / 7 / 10) — this killed balanced double brooms, capped ell_2 - ell_3 <= 5 for all spiders, and forced max pendant <= 7 for broom-handles, uniformly in n. (2) Next lever, finite and cheap: cap M_r for r-fold unions of structured sumsets (the window above the (r+1)-st arm reach); polynomial M_r propagates the near-tie down the whole arm hierarchy, making every multi-arm tree's second-tier reaches equal to within O(M_p) while ell_1 = N - ell_2 — then the vertex budget (arms are Golomb rulers: an arm of reach ~ell needs enough vertices, and n - 1 edges total) plus the pole-cover bound 2 sqrt(2q+1) on how many arms can carry the top q values should close spiders and multi-brooms entirely. (3) In parallel, the general-tree reduction: if both deep tips are thin (path/broom-like within weighted distance ~10), the caps force a near-diameter pair INSIDE one side — a descent that terminates in either a thick tip (branching near the extremes, costing vertices and colliding with degree/Sidon bounds) or a capped configuration. The realistic milestone ordering: (a) publish the double-broom/spider/broom-handle exclusions now (first order-independent family kills beyond stars and paths; note-grade already, and they strictly generalize Lemma 4a via the crowding bound nu(q) <= sqrt(2q+1)); (b) run the r=3 union-tiling search; (c) formalize the descent to get 'no Leech tree with both deep tips thin', reducing the SWZ conjecture's open middle to thick-tipped few-pole trees, where the star-Sidon S(d) growth and the waste-merge inequality (balanced heavy cut forces ~n^4/32 waste but thick bushy shapes cannot supply long-hop pairs) are the natural closers.

summary: Additive-combinatorics lens on Leech trees: hardened and machine-checked the session's difference-set obstruction, then mapped exactly how far single-vertex additive arguments can go. Core proved results: (1) a Master Lemma — at any vertex v of any tree with all pairwise distances distinct (DI), augmenting the branches with D_0={0} for v itself, the sum map {x,y} -> a_x+a_y is injective on all cross-branch pairs, its values are exactly the cross distances, and in a Leech tree these together with the within-branch distance multisets tile [1,N] exactly; the session's leaf lemma, the pairwise disjointness of branch difference sets, and full-size cross difference sets D_i-D_j all fall out as one-line corollaries (machine-checked at every vertex of all 5 known Leech trees and 200 random DI trees). (2) A barrier theorem: the complete single-vertex axiom set is SATISFIABLE at exact Leech parameters (explicit witness D_1={1..m}, D_2={2m,...,2m^2} at N=2m^2+m for every m), so no proof of nonexistence can come from single-vertex depth/cross-sum axioms alone — the counting constant is exactly c=1/4 (centroid, tight on double brooms) with identity ceiling c=1/2, both unreachable as contradictions. (3) The way past the barrier: a computable profile obstruction M*(n_1..n_r) generalizing the repo's star-Sidon minima S(d)=M*(1^d); exhaustive validated DFS gives M*(4,2)=42>36=N(9) and M*(5,2)>55=N(11) — the first analytic-style kills of non-star branch profiles (no DI tree of order 9 resp. 11 has a vertex with four resp. five size-2 branches), a new filter family for the open orders 25,27. (4) A difference-coincidence classification lemma yielding a rigidity dichotomy (either some branch is large or the branch depth sets are massively mirror-correlated), which assembles into a concrete proof skeleton (sketch status) for 'no vertex of a large Leech tree has all branches of size <= 2'. (5) Literature: Ruzsa's weak-Sidon interval bound immediately improves the asymptotic degree bound to Delta <= n/2 + O(sqrt n); PSDS nonexistence (no components of size >= 6) supplies the window-counting method needed to make M* asymptotic. Honest negative: the energy/BSG route caps at |A-A| >~ n^{3/2} and cannot reach a contradiction at a single vertex; the middle regime (every vertex has a big branch) provably needs recursion or multi-vertex arguments.
