claims.name: Master Lemma (augmented cross-branch sum injectivity)
claims.statement: Let T be any positively edge-weighted tree on n vertices in which all C(n,2) pairwise path-distances are distinct (any Leech tree qualifies). Fix any vertex v. Let T_1,...,T_r be the components of T-v, a_x=d(v,x) for x!=v, a_v=0, and view v as an augmented 0-th branch with depth set D_0={0}, D_i={a_x : x in T_i}. Call an unordered pair {x,y} of distinct vertices CROSS if x,y lie in different augmented branches (this includes every pair {v,x}). Then: (i) the map {x,y} -> a_x+a_y is injective on cross pairs; (ii) its values are exactly the distances of cross pairs, hence distinct from d(x',y') for every within-branch pair {x',y'}; (iii) in a Leech tree all cross values lie in [1,N] and (cross values) disjoint-union (within-branch distance multisets of the T_i) = {1,...,N} exactly, each value once. In particular all n-1 depths are distinct and distinct from every proper cross sum. This strengthens the repo's Lemma 5(a) (one vertex per branch) to all vertices of all branches simultaneously, and the D_0 augmentation removes every corner case (v itself, leaves of v) from the session's leaf lemma.
claims.proof_sketch: One line, routing injectivity through the distance map: for a cross pair the v-x and v-y paths meet only at v, so d(x,y)=a_x+a_y; distinct cross pairs are distinct vertex pairs, hence have distinct distances by distance-injectivity; within-branch pairs are different pairs again, so their distances differ from all cross values. (iii) is the bijection {pairs}->{1..N} split by whether the path passes through v. Machine-checked at every vertex of the 5 known Leech trees and 200 random distance-injective trees, n=8..13 (ac_checks.py, all pass).
claims.checkable_prediction: At every vertex of every distance-injective weighted tree, the (n-1) + sum_{i<j} n_i n_j augmented cross values are pairwise distinct; in a Leech tree they tile [1,N] jointly with the within-branch distances. Verifiable by the provided script on any tree.

claims.name: Difference-set package (hardened leaf lemma; disjoint branch difference sets)
claims.statement: Same setting. (a) For all 0<=i<j<=r: (D_i - D_i) intersect (D_j - D_j) = {0} — the nonzero within-branch difference sets are PAIRWISE DISJOINT across branches. (b) For i!=j: |D_i - D_j| = n_i n_j (all cross differences between one fixed pair of branches are distinct). (c) Hardened session leaf lemma: with B = pendant edge weights at v (depth sets of the singleton branches) and A* = {0} union {a_x : x neither v nor a pendant leaf of v}: all elements of A* union B are distinct, (A*-A*) intersect (B-B) = {0}, and B is weak Sidon. (d) Caveat, exactly delimiting the obstruction: cross differences taken from DIFFERENT branch-pairs (i,j),(k,l) MAY coincide when i=l or j=k, and within-branch sums are entirely unconstrained — so the full depth set A is only cross-branch Sidon, not Sidon.
claims.proof_sketch: Each part is a rearrangement into an equality of two cross-pair sums: e.g. for (a), a-a'=b-b' nonzero with a,a' in D_i, b,b' in D_j gives a+b'=a'+b with {x_a,y_b'} != {x_a',y_b} two distinct cross pairs (branch disjointness forces componentwise equality), contradicting the Master Lemma. The D_0 augmentation makes v-involving and pendant-leaf cases automatic. Part (d) is verified by explicit failure analysis: the rearranged pairs can land inside one branch, where sums are not distances. Machine-checked (ac_checks.py; coincidence.py found zero unclassified coincidences).
claims.checkable_prediction: On any DI tree, for every vertex, intersecting any two branches' nonzero difference sets returns empty; the provided classifier finds every cross-difference coincidence chargeable to a 3AP or a within-branch pair (0 'forbidden' events in all runs).

claims.name: Single-vertex counting constant is exactly c=1/4, ceiling 1/2 (vacuous as a bound)
claims.statement: The counting consequence of the Master Lemma, N >= (n-1) + sum_{i<j} n_i n_j, is an identity minus sum_i C(n_i,2) >= 0 and hence vacuous. The guaranteed-over-all-trees value of max_v [(n-1)+sum_{i<j} n_i n_j] is (1/4+o(1))n^2 (centroid: max branch <= n/2 gives sum_{i<j} n_i n_j >= (n-1)(n-1-n/2)/2; balanced paths/double brooms attain ~n^2/4 at their best vertex, so 1/4 is exact); the identity ceiling n^2/2 is attained only at star centers. Kovari-Sos-Turan-type counting on the cross-sum bipartite structure cannot improve this: see the Barrier theorem.
claims.proof_sketch: Bookkeeping from the exact partition identity: pairs through v number (n-1)+sum_{i<j} n_i n_j and total pairs number N. The centroid bound is Cauchy-Schwarz on sum n_i^2 <= max_i n_i * (n-1); tightness by computing the profile of a balanced double broom (every vertex has a branch of size >= ~n/2).

claims.name: Barrier theorem: single-vertex additive axioms are satisfiable at exact Leech parameters
claims.statement: For every m>=2 set n=2m+1, N=n(n-1)/2=2m^2+m. The abstract system D_1={1,...,m}, D_2={2m,4m,...,2m^2} satisfies EVERY single-vertex conclusion available from the Master Lemma and its corollaries: 2m distinct depths; all m^2 cross sums distinct, distinct from the depths, and contained in [1,N] with maximum exactly N; branch difference sets disjoint; and the leftover set [1,N] minus (depths union cross sums) has exactly 2*C(m,2) elements — precisely the two branches' within-distance budget, which the axioms leave unconstrained. Consequently NO nonexistence proof for large n can be derived from the single-vertex depth/cross-sum axioms alone (not even adding the exact-tiling counting): any proof must invoke within-branch realizability (e.g. the meet-depth lemma below), several vertices simultaneously, global moment identities, or profile obstructions at bushier vertices. This definitively answers 'can f(n) be pushed superquadratic': not from these axioms — they are satisfiable at c=1/2 exactly.
claims.proof_sketch: Direct verification: depths distinct since m<2m; cross sums 2mj+i are distinct by base-2m digits and are not depths (nonzero residue in [1,m] and magnitude > m rules out D_1; residue rules out D_2); max cross sum 2m^2+m=N; count N-(m^2+2m)=m^2-m=2*C(m,2). Verified programmatically for m=2..14 (ac_checks.py section B). Note the witness even realizes N as its top value, as a Leech tree must.
claims.checkable_prediction: The explicit witness passes any independent implementation of the axiom checks at every m; no single-vertex additive filter derived from the Master Lemma alone can kill the balanced-two-branch profile.

claims.name: Profile obstruction M*: computable generalization of star-Sidon, with first non-star kills (orders 9 and 11)
claims.statement: For a branch profile (n_1,...,n_r) let M*(n_1..n_r) be the minimum over abstract systems (disjoint depth sets of sizes n_i; all augmented cross sums distinct and distinct from depths) of the maximum occurring value. If a DI tree of order n = 1+sum n_i has a vertex with that profile then M* <= N; M* is monotone under taking sub-profiles. M*(1^d) = S(d), the repo's star-Sidon minima. Computed by exhaustive iterative-deepening DFS (validated by reproducing S(4)=11, S(5)=19, S(6)=31): M*(2,2)=8<=10, M*(2^3 with s... (r,s)=(3,2))=20<=21, M*(3,3)=41<=45, M*((2,3) bipartite)=15<=21 — all feasible, with r=2 profiles packing PERFECTLY (excess 0, matching the Barrier witness) — but M*(2,2,2,2)=42 > 36=N(9) and M*(2,2,2,2,2) > 55=N(11) (caps 50-55 all exhausted infeasible, 13.5M nodes). KILLS: no distance-injective tree of order 9 (resp. 11) has a vertex with four (resp. five) branches of size 2 — the first analytic-style exclusions of non-star profiles, purely additive, independent of branch topology and of the exhaustive order-9/11 searches. The excess M*-Q over the counting bound Q grows superlinearly in r at fixed s (s=1: 0,0,1,4,10 for r=2..6; s=2: 0,2,10,>=23 for r=2..5), while the Leech slack is only N-Q = rs(s-1)/2, linear in r.
claims.proof_sketch: The relaxation is valid because within-branch values are unconstrained by the axioms and the value budget [1,N] is exact. DFS: elements placed in increasing order with canonical part-opening, pruning on any collision among depths/cross-sums and on sums exceeding the cap; exhaustive at each cap. Validated against three independently known star values and the perfect r=2 packings. Machine-proof status: exhaustive computation (mstar.py/mstar2.py/mstar3.py); an independent reimplementation is recommended before publication, matching repo practice for S(d).
claims.checkable_prediction: Any correct independent search will find: no 8-element system with four 2-element parts fits in [1,41], but [[1,11],[4,8],[6,12],[21,30]] fits in [1,42]; and no 10-element five-part system fits in [1,55]. Prediction for the open program: M*(r,2) > 2r^2+r for ALL r>=4, and profile filters at n=25 (e.g. computing M*(2^12) vs 300) will kill topologies the current F1-F6 filters miss.

claims.name: Meet-depth injectivity: pointwise bound on the sum-representation function (beyond the barrier)
claims.statement: T DI, v any vertex, A = depth set. For a within-branch pair {x,y} let m(x,y) be the vertex where the paths v->x and v->y separate; then d(x,y) = a_x + a_y - 2*a_{m(x,y)} and the map {x,y} -> (a_x+a_y, a_{m(x,y)}) is INJECTIVE on within-branch pairs. Hence for every integer sigma, the number of unordered pairs of distinct non-v vertices with a_x+a_y=sigma satisfies r_A(sigma) <= 1 + #{a in A : 2a < sigma} (the 1 is the unique cross pair; each within representation consumes a distinct feasible meet depth). This is the first proved constraint coupling the unconstrained within-branch sums to the tree — i.e., strictly beyond the Barrier axioms — and is usable as a propagation rule in weight-level searches (it limits how many small depths can coexist with many small pair-sums).
claims.proof_sketch: The distance identity is standard; injectivity: two within pairs with the same (sigma, mu) would have the same distance sigma-2mu, contradicting distance-injectivity; mu ranges over A (meets lie inside branches). Machine-checked at every vertex of all known Leech trees and 200 random DI trees, including the pointwise inequality (ac_checks.py check 5).
claims.checkable_prediction: On any DI tree, no two within-branch pairs at the same vertex share both pair-sum and meet-depth; r_A(sigma) never exceeds 1 + |A intersect [1,(sigma-1)/2]|.

claims.name: Difference-coincidence classification and the symmetry-rigidity dichotomy
claims.statement: Classification (proved): at any vertex of a DI tree, whenever two DISTINCT cross pairs satisfy a_x-a_y = a_u-a_w != 0, either they share an element (3AP; then the outer pair is a within-branch pair, or is THE unique cross pair whose sum is twice the center's depth — at most one per center), or the rearranged pairs {x,w},{u,y} include at least one within-branch pair; two disjoint reps whose rearrangements are both cross are impossible. Quantitative corollary (proved): all branches but at most one lie entirely in [1,N/2] (two depths > N/2 in different branches would give a distance > N). Writing b for the number of those depths, W = sum of their within-pair counts, Y = number of unordered pairs of equal-sum within-branch pairs lying in DIFFERENT branches, and I = sum_i C(C(n_i,2),2): C(b,2) - [b + 3W + 2Y + I] <= N/2 - 1. Dichotomy: since C(b,2) ~ n^2/2 and N/2 ~ n^2/4, any vertex with all branches of size <= s (so W <= bs/2, I <= b s^3/8, b >= n-1-s) forces Y >= n^2/8 - O(n s^3) — a positive fraction of ALL pairs of within-branch pairs must collide in sum, i.e., the branch depth sets are massively mirror-correlated around a common center. The five known Leech trees sit at the opposite extreme: Y = 0 at every vertex of every one of them (checked).
claims.proof_sketch: Classification is the Master Lemma applied to the rearranged sum equality, with the corner cases enumerated; verified exhaustively (coincidence.py: 0 forbidden events over all vertices of the 5 known trees and 60 random DI trees, all coincidences falling in the three chargeable classes). The inequality is pigeonhole on distinct difference values of the bottom-half depths in [1,N/2-1], with the coincidence mass bounded class by class: 3AP-cross <= 1 per center; each within pair's sum matches at most one cross sum (cross sums distinct) and at most one doubled depth; equal within-sums in different branches contribute 2 coincidences each; internal-to-one-branch coincidences <= I; both-cross disjoint is impossible.
claims.checkable_prediction: Y=0 at every vertex of every known Leech tree (verified by ycheck.py); on random DI trees the classifier never finds an unclassifiable coincidence. If an order-25 Leech tree exists with a vertex whose branches are all small, its branch depth sets must exhibit the mirror-correlation (testable filter).

claims.name: Asymptotic hedgehog kill (proof skeleton): no vertex with all branches of size <= 2 for large n
claims.statement: CONJECTURED THEOREM with an explicit elementary proof program: for all sufficiently large n, no Leech tree of order n has a vertex all of whose branches have at most 2 vertices; equivalently every vertex sees a branch with >= 3 vertices. (Extends the star exclusions — the s=1 row — to s=2; empirically the kill already starts at 4-5 branches: M*(2^4)>N(9), M*(2^5)>N(11).) Skeleton: (1) by the dichotomy, Y >= n^2/8-O(n) while Y <= C(rho,2) <= (n-1)^2/8 (rho = number of size-2 branches <= (n-1)/2), so rho = n/2-o(n), nearly all branches have size exactly 2, and Y is within O(n) of its maximum; convexity then forces all but O(1) branches to share ONE common within-sum sigma_0. (2) The shallow depths alpha_i of that class are weak Sidon (their pairwise sums are distinct cross sums) and lie in [1,sigma_0/2], so Ruzsa's bound gives sigma_0 >= 2(n/2)^2(1-o(1)) = N(1-o(1)). (3) The deep depths beta_i = sigma_0-alpha_i give cross sums beta_i+beta_j = 2 sigma_0-(alpha_i+alpha_j) <= N, forcing all alpha's into an interval of length o(n^2) around N/2 — where a weak Sidon set of size n/2(1-o(1)) cannot fit (it needs length n^2/4(1-o(1))). Contradiction. Every constant is marginal (Leech is a perfect packing), so dotting the o(1) bookkeeping IS the remaining work; steps use only the proved classification, convexity, and the cited weak-Sidon bound.
claims.proof_sketch: As in the statement; the fragile points, checked once each here but needing careful writing: the exact coincidence budget in step (1) including mixed size-1/size-2 profiles (singletons contribute no within pairs, which only sharpens the pigeonhole and forces rho maximal); the concentration lemma (Y >= C(rho,2)-O(n) with sum m_sigma = rho implies a class of size rho-O(1), by m*(rho-m*) <= O(n)); and the two applications of the weak-Sidon interval bound with its O(M^{1/4}) error, which is far below the n^2-scale gaps used. The squeeze has real room: interval length O(n^{3/2}) available vs n^2/4 required.
claims.checkable_prediction: M*(2^r) > 2r^2+r for every r >= 4 (verified r=4,5; each additional r is a finite computation); no Leech tree of any order has a vertex with >= 4 size-2 branches and only size-<=2 branches — testable against every future search survivor list.

claims.name: Asymptotic degree bound Delta <= n/2 + O(sqrt n) via Ruzsa's weak-Sidon bound
claims.statement: In any Leech tree of order n, the maximum degree satisfies Delta <= sqrt(N/2) + O(N^{1/4}) = n/2 + O(sqrt n), improving the ~0.707n asymptotic implicit in the repo's star-Sidon analysis. Proof: the incident weights at a degree-d vertex are star-Sidon (repo Lemma 5b, proved); the two largest sum to a distance <= N, so the d-1 smallest incident weights lie in [1, N/2] and form a weak Sidon set; apply the weak-Sidon interval bound f(M) <= sqrt(M) + O(M^{1/4}) (Ruzsa; constant improved in 'A note on weak Sidon sequences'). Not useful at n=18 (gives ~13 vs the exhaustive 11) — strictly asymptotic. Possible overlap with the paywalled Luo-Yu 2024 improvement of the SWZ degree bound (their abstract cites Sidon sets; text inaccessible per the repo's literature ledger) — check before claiming novelty.
claims.proof_sketch: Three proved ingredients chained: star-Sidon at a vertex (repo, machine-checked), the halving trick (two elements > N/2 across the top pair would exceed N), and the literature theorem on weak Sidon sets — the one imported, clearly-labeled LITERATURE step.

claims.name: Literature findings (task 3) and the energy/BSG negative result (task 4)
claims.statement: (a) Weak Sidon / well-spread sets: maximum size in [0,M] is sqrt(M)+O(M^{1/4}) (Ruzsa 1993 via linear-equation solvability; alternate proof with constant ~sqrt 2 in 'A note on weak Sidon sequences'); Erdos's $500 question on the o(M^{1/4}) error remains open. (b) Ma-Tang 2026 (arXiv 2602.23282): every weak Sidon set of size n contains a Sidon subset of size ceil((n+1)/2), and this is TIGHT — the exact transfer cost between our weak-Sidon structures and strict-Sidon tools. (c) Perfect systems of difference sets (Bermond-Kotzig-Turgeon; 2025 survey arXiv 2510.20446): NO (m,k,c)-PSDS exists with component size k >= 6; Kotzig-Turgeon 1980 prove every perfect system has small components; their window/top-fraction counting method is the right tool for proving M* lower bounds analytically; our spider reformulation (legs = Golomb rulers whose difference sets, together with the cross-sum system, exactly tile [1,N]) is a hybrid PSDS/multipartite-B2+ object that appears unstudied. (d) 'Half-Sidon implies large difference set': no off-the-shelf theorem found; BSG runs the wrong direction (large energy -> structure), and here cross-injectivity makes energy small and |A+A| >= n^2/4 large for free, while Ruzsa's triangle inequality yields only |A-A| >= sqrt(|A||A+A|) ~ n^{3/2} against the available room 2N ~ n^2 — confirming the context's assessment that the energy route cannot close at a single vertex; the meet-depth lemma is what replaces it. Sources: [Ruzsa's problem on Bi-Sidon sets](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.03128), [Largest Sidon subsets in weak Sidon sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23282), [A note on weak Sidon sequences](https://www.academia.edu/86245556/A_note_on_weak_Sidon_sequences), [PSDS survey](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20446), [Regular perfect systems of difference sets](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0012365X77900644), [BSG formalization](https://www.isa-afp.org/entries/Balog_Szemeredi_Gowers.html), [Dense Sidon subsets discussion](https://gowers.wordpress.com/2012/07/13/what-are-dense-sidon-subsets-of-12-n-like/).
claims.proof_sketch: Literature claims as reported by the cited sources (the k>=6 PSDS nonexistence and the Ma-Tang theorem were read from the papers' own statements; exact constants in the Ruzsa bound not re-derived here). The negative energy assessment is proved-as-stated: r(sigma) <= 1 + r_within(sigma) with r_within bounded only by the meet-depth lemma; even a perfect Sidon depth set gives |A+A| = C(n-1,2) < 2N, so no single-vertex energy contradiction is possible.

summary: Two new computer-verified nonexistence results at the smallest open orders, a validated search toolkit, and machine-checked structural lemmas. (1) SPIDERS CLOSED: no Leech tree of order 25 or 27 is a path or a spider; the same top-down "zero-slack" prover closes every admissible order through 51 (25, 27, 36, 38, 49, 51 — each with a full from-scratch paranoid recheck at every node), so combined with Taylor's parity condition and the known exhaustions (n<=18), NO spider or path Leech tree exists for ANY order 5 <= n <= 63. Total cost: 236,957 search nodes for all six orders — versus 6e10 nodes for the bottom-up n=18 exhaustion alone. (2) BI-SPIDERS CLOSED AT 25 AND 27: no Leech tree of order 25 or 27 has at most two vertices of degree >= 3 (covers all double stars and double brooms); C prover differential-validated against a Python reference (exact branch/node/solution agreement n=4..13, positive controls find exactly the known trees incl. the L6 double star), n=25: 29,155,730 nodes x3 identical replicas, n=27: 45,862,384 nodes in 3 exactly-partitioning shards, 0 solutions. (3) CATERPILLARS: the bottom-up forced-forest search restricted to caterpillar shape is validated three ways and exhausts n<=16 (finds exactly the known trees), but measured level growth at n=25 (level 13 already 3.3e9 nodes, growing x9.5-10 per level with 11 levels to go) shows bottom-up exhaustion needs >=1e16 nodes — infeasible; caterpillar orders 25/27 remain OPEN, and the obstruction is identified precisely: a pendant leaf carries two coordinates (rho, lam) with a free radius b, so top-down window forcing pins only one coordinate per end-cluster leaf. Proved theory: caterpillar ghost-coordinate reformulation, global coordinate distinctness, a hardened pendant-difference disjointness lemma for all distinct-distance trees, and a new two-sided window-tiling lemma with excess E (de Bruijn-type end rigidity; E in {0,1,2} on the known trees, E=1 on L6 via the same-leaf degenerate case) — all machine-checked; self-contained rederivations of the classical path and star kills; explicit bounds (order 25: hop diameter <=19, spine <=18, >=7 leaves; order 27: <=20, <=19, >=8). KEY EMPIRICAL DISCOVERY pointing at a general theorem: the spider prover's case tree per anchor branch is ~110-130 nodes and its value window never exceeds depth 22 below N, INDEPENDENT of n (checked at n=12, 18, 25, 51) — the closure is a bounded n-independent case analysis in disguise, so a symbolic uniformization would yield "no spider Leech tree for any n >= 5", the first infinite structured-family nonexistence theorem for the Szekely-Wang-Zhang conjecture. claims.name: L-A: Caterpillar ghost-coordinate reformulation
claims.statement: Let T be a caterpillar with spine v_1..v_m (its non-leaf vertices, which form a path), p_i = d(v_1,v_i); for each leaf u attached at v_{i(u)} by pendant weight b_u set rho(u) = p_{i(u)} + b_u and lam(u) = p_{i(u)} - b_u; for spine vertices rho(v_i) = lam(v_i) = p_i. Then for ALL distinct vertices x,y with i(x) <= i(y): d(x,y) = rho(y) - lam(x) (both orientations agree when i(x) = i(y)). Hence T is Leech iff the C(n,2) admissible differences rho(y) - lam(x) are exactly {1,...,N}.
claims.proof_sketch: The x-y path descends the pendant edge of x (contributing b_x = rho(x) - p_{i(x)}, or 0 for spine x), runs along the spine (p_{i(y)} - p_{i(x)}), and climbs to y (b_y): total (p_{i(y)} + b_y) - (p_{i(x)} - b_x) = rho(y) - lam(x). Machine-checked on the five known Leech trees and 2281 random distinct-distance caterpillars.

claims.name: L-B: Global coordinate distinctness in caterpillars
claims.statement: In any caterpillar whose pairwise distances are all distinct (in particular any Leech caterpillar), the n values rho(x) are pairwise distinct and the n values lam(x) are pairwise distinct. Equivalently: for leaves u != u' at spine vertices v_i, v_{i'}, the pendant-weight difference b_u - b_{u'} never equals +(p_{i'} - p_i) or -(p_{i'} - p_i), and no pendant weight b_u equals a spine distance from its attach vertex.
claims.proof_sketch: rho(x) = d(v_1, x) and distances from the fixed vertex v_1 are values of distinct pairs, hence distinct (rho(v_1) = 0 is below all). Symmetrically lam(x) = p_m - d(x, v_m). A coincidence gamma_u = gamma_{u'} would give d(u, v_j) = d(u', v_j) for the common right spine vertex j = max(i, i'), two distinct pairs with equal distance. Machine-checked (same script).

claims.name: L-C: Pendant-interior difference disjointness (hardened key structural fact)
claims.statement: Let T be ANY tree with all pairwise distances distinct. Fix a vertex v with pendant leaves u_1..u_k (pendant weights B = {b_1..b_k}) and let A = {0} u {d(v,x) : x != v, x not a pendant leaf at v}. Then (A - A) n (B - B) = {0}: no nonzero difference of two pendant weights at v equals a difference of two elements of A (taking 0 in A: pendant-weight differences also avoid every distance from v to a non-pendant vertex).
claims.proof_sketch: Suppose d(v,x) - d(v,y) = b_j - b_i != 0 (x or y may be v itself via 0 in A). Since u_i is a leaf whose only neighbour is v, d(x, u_i) = d(x,v) + b_i = d(y,v) + b_j = d(y, u_j). The pairs (x,u_i) and (y,u_j) are distinct — x != y because b_i != b_j, u_i != u_j, and x,y avoid the pendant set — contradicting distinctness of the distance multiset. This hardens the session's (A-A)/(B-B) fact with exact quantifiers and no Leech assumption beyond distinct distances. Machine-checked on 3000 random distinct-distance trees and the five known Leech trees.
claims.checkable_prediction: Same script: for every vertex of every generated tree it verifies (B-B) avoids (A-A).

claims.name: L-D: Two-sided window tiling with excess (new)
claims.statement: Let T be a Leech caterpillar, A1 = max rho, G1 = min lam, E = (A1 - G1) - N. Then E >= 0, and with delta(x) = A1 - rho(x) >= 0, eps(x) = lam(x) - G1 >= 0: for EVERY s in {0,...,N-1} there is EXACTLY one unordered pair x != y (orientation i(x) <= i(y)) with eps(x) + delta(y) = s + E, and no pair has eps + delta < E. Consequently the near-extreme offset sets delta, eps restricted to the initial window form an exact unique-representation additive cover of {E, E+1, ..., E+c} for as long as only end-cluster vertices participate — a de Bruijn/digit-system rigidity on the two ends of the caterpillar. E > 0 occurs iff the two extremes are not an admissible pair; on the known trees E = 0 (n=4 path), 1 (n=3 path; L6), 2 (n=4 star). For L6 both extremes are the SAME leaf (pendant weight 8): A1 = 13, G1 = -3, E = 1, delta = {13,8,12,11,4,0}, eps = {3,8,2,1,4,0}, and every s = 0..14 has a unique admissible representation eps + delta = s + 1.
claims.proof_sketch: By L-A the value of an admissible pair is (A1 - G1) - eps(x) - delta(y); the Leech property makes each value N - s occur exactly once. Machine-checked: the script asserts the unique-representation property for every s on each known Leech caterpillar. The rigidity content (interval factorizations = mixed-radix digit systems) is what a caterpillar proof should exploit; see the caterpillar-obstruction claim for why this alone does not close.

claims.name: No Leech path for n >= 5 (classical, rederived self-contained)
claims.statement: For every n >= 5 no path on n vertices admits a Leech labelling (equivalently: no perfect Golomb ruler with >= 5 marks). Literature: Leech 1975 (noted), SWZ 2005, Calhoun 2007 Prop 1.2; ledger L3.
claims.proof_sketch: A Leech path is a ruler 0 = x_1 < ... < x_n = N with all differences distinct hence exactly {1..N}. Realizing N-1 forces (after reflection) first gap g_1 = 1; realizing N-2 then forces last gap g_{n-1} = 2 (all alternatives repeat a gap); N-3 is automatically d(x_2, x_{n-1}); realizing N-4 forces g_2 = 3; then N-5 has NO realizer: it needs prefix+suffix = 5 with prefixes {0,1,4,...} and suffixes {0,2,...}, and each completion (g_{n-2} in {2,3}, g_3 = 1, g_2 in {1,2}) repeats an existing gap. n = 5, 6 close by the same forcing with boundary identifications. Independently re-confirmed computationally here: paths are included in the spider searches, which close at every order 5 <= n <= 63.

claims.name: Top-down zero-slack prover: soundness, completeness, termination
claims.statement: The algorithm of theory-lab/catspider/spider_topdown.py — branch on the integer anchor T (N/2 < T <= N-1, T' = N - T pinned as second tip); descend v = N-1..1 over the value ladder, maintaining pinned marks and the set of realized pair values; when v is unrealized, branch over ALL ways to realize it by adding one or two new marks (center partner, pinned partner, or both new; same-leg differences and cross-leg sums; existing or fresh legs), pruning any duplicate/out-of-range value and any state with more than n-1 marks — terminates, and: (a) any state reaching v = 0 is a Leech spider of order n; (b) every Leech spider or path of order n survives down the branch T = its largest tip until found; (c) hence closure of all branches proves nonexistence at order n. The analogous statements hold for the bi-spider prover (two centers joined by a spine of length Q; anchor cases LR: T_L + Q + T_R = N with T_L < T_R, and LL: T_1 + T_2 = N with 1 <= Q <= T_2 - 1, RR covered by mirror symmetry; vertex budget n-2).
claims.proof_sketch: Soundness: pinned pair values are kept distinct in [1,N], so |values| = C(m+1,2) exactly with m marks; at v = 0 all of {1..N} is covered, so C(m+1,2) >= N forces m = n-1 and the state is a full weighted spider whose distance multiset is exactly {1..N} (re-verified from scratch by the paranoid recomputation at every node). Completeness: for a hypothetical Leech spider S consistent with the state, the realizer pair of v has at most two unpinned endpoints; an exhaustive case check (center pair; same-leg difference with 0/1/2 unpinned marks; cross-leg sum with 0/1/2 unpinned marks; each on existing or fresh legs) shows every configuration is generated by an enumerated option, and S's marks satisfy all caps. A mutation test confirms the one option family not exercised by the positive controls (same-leg differences) is live: disabling it changes node counts (254->253 at n=8, 971->970 at n=10, 2050->2049 at n=12). Bi-spider: leaves are exactly the leg tips (spine interior has degree 2), so the value-N pair is tip-tip of type LL, LR, or RR; |values| = C(m+2,2).

claims.name: C1. Subforest invariant and attachment lemma for diameter <= 4
claims.statement: Let T be a tree of hop-diameter <= 4 and c a vertex of hop-eccentricity <= 2 (one always exists). Conversely (v) every weighted forest satisfying (i)-(ii) extends to a weighted tree of hop-diameter <= 4.
claims.proof_sketch: Tree paths are unique. For (iii): d_hop(c,l), d_hop(c,l') <= 2; if c not in {p,q}, c is adjacent to p or q or hangs off l or l', each giving a vertex at hop distance >= 3 from c. Two diameter >= 3 components would need c inside both disjoint vertex sets. For (iv): a vertex s != c at hop 2 from c with degree >= 2 has a neighbour at hop 3. For (v): attach every star centre to c (stars have centre eccentricity 1, so their leaves land at hop 2).

claims.name: C7. Master generating identity for diameter <= 4 (exact power-sum repackaging)

Hence det J is identically zero iff n is a power of 2 (n = 4, 8, 16, ...), and for all other n it is nonzero whenever the weights are distinct. claims.name: C12. Transfer to diameter 5 and to spiders; precise breaking point of the window method

(iii) The method survives for every tree whose branches at the centre contain at most one branching vertex (star branches: one meet class; path branches: differences; broom branches: two classes, constants doubled). claims.name: C13. Assessment: what the power-sum overdetermination can and cannot give
claims.statement: For a fixed topology the Leech condition is equivalent to the infinite power-sum system, and by C11 the first n-1 equations are already generically 0-dimensional (with the classified star exception); each existing Leech tree is a rigid isolated solution. However (i) per-(n, topology) decidability is trivial anyway (weights are bounded by N+1-c_e), (ii) over the reals the higher moments add nothing beyond majorization (Schur-convexity, as recorded in the repo's theory notes), and (iii) parametrised families of growing order have ~n unknowns, so the system is never 'few-parameter' unless structural rigidity (the additive combinatorics of C5-C9) reduces it first. Conclusion: the power-sum lens contributes rigidity statements, exact identities (C7) usable as redundant constraints in CP-SAT/SAT models, and the star classification C10, but uniform-in-n nonexistence must come from integer additive structure, not from the moment system.

best_route: Two-track route to 'no Leech trees of hop-diameter <= 4 beyond the five known', then outward.
